title: Post-Incident Reassurance Kit — Timelines, Evidence and Messaging
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact kit for customer-facing teams to use after a significant inference disruption. Focus: quick, factual reassurance that (1) explains what happened, (2) demonstrates corrective action with evidence, and (3) outlines next steps and what customers can expect going forward.

Audience:
- Customer success / account managers
- Sales leads handling inbound questions
- Support reps drafting status emails
- Executive comms for key accounts

How to use this doc:
- Pick a timeline template that matches severity (S1 vs S2)
- Attach proof (link to dashboard slice, error logs, and runbook entry)
- Customize one of the short templates below for the specific customer and channel (email, chat, status page, post-mortem brief)

Key principles (short):
- Be concrete: state the impact window, affected regions/services, and mitigation steps we ran.
- Show instrumentation: include one chart or metric snapshot (error rate, median latency, token throughput) with timestamps.
- Empathy + ownership: apologize, explain, and commit to follow-up with a clear timeline.
- Avoid speculation: if root cause unknown, say we are investigating and give a target update time.

Quick timeline templates (pick one):
1) Rapid recovery (<= 2 hours)
- 00:00 UTC: Alerts detected for increased 5xxs on hosted-api-us-east-1
- 00:09 UTC: Automatic routing shifted to dedicated-pool-02 (failover executed)
- 00:12 UTC: Error rate reduced to baseline; median gen latency returned to normal
- 00:30 UTC: Engineering rollback of recent kernel change completed
- Customer message: Incident contained, traffic restored, follow-up post-mortem scheduled within 72 hours

2) Multi-region switchover (2–8 hours)
- 02:15 UTC: Elevated tail latency observed in eu-west and us-west regions
- 02:25 UTC: Smart-routing policy enacted to route EU traffic to eu-central-2 with warmed cache
- 03:05 UTC: Partial degradation remained for long-context models; temporary recommendation: reduce max_tokens for critical routes
- 07:20 UTC: Full throughput restored after autoscale and kernel fallback
- Customer message: We rerouted traffic and applied temporary config to preserve availability; detailed timeline and root-cause in post-mortem

3) Extended outage (> 8 hours)
- 00:00 UTC: Incident declared S1; incident commander assigned
- 01:00 UTC: Surface-level mitigation (circuit breaker, capacity isolation) brought partial relief
- 06:00 UTC: Coordinated cross-region capacity rebalancing
- 14:00 UTC: Service restored; rolling validation for 24 hours recommended
- Customer message: Apology, what we fixed, what we’re doing to prevent recurrence, compensation or credits if applicable

Evidence checklist (short snippets customers want to see):
- Before/after error-rate snapshot (5xx counts, percent of requests failing) with timestamps
- Latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99) for affected routes during window
- Confirmation of fall-forward action: which model variant/quantization/region we routed to and why
- Rollback/patch commit id and link to PR (if code change involved)
- Ticket numbers for follow-up and post-mortem link (Confluence/Jira)

Suggested language blocks (pick/trim for length):
1) Short status (customer-facing):
"We experienced a targeted service disruption that affected text-generation requests in region X between 02:15–03:05 UTC. Our runtime automatically rerouted traffic to a healthy region and applied a temporary configuration to keep critical requests running. We resolved the immediate issue and are now running a full investigation. We will share a detailed post-mortem within 72 hours. We regret the interruption and are committed to preventing recurrence."

2) Tactical technical note (for platform/ops-savvy customers):
"Root cause appears related to a kernel selection path introduced in the 2026-02-xx runtime rollout. During peak contiguous long-sequence traffic, that code path caused excessive memory fragmentation and request queuing. Mitigation steps: we rolled back the kernel selector and triggered smart-routing to warm cache in eu-central-2. We have a PR with additional checks to gate the selector behind a canary flag. Ref: github PR-274, JIRA-8123."

3) Compensation/prestige note (for enterprise accounts):
"We will apply a service credit for the impacted window and schedule a technical review with your engineering/design lead to go through the incident and recommended config changes. If you'd like a dedicated post-mortem call, we can arrange that within the next 5 business days."

Dos and don’ts (short):
- Do: Attach a visual (simple PNG) showing error-rate and latency change with timestamps
- Do: Offer a concrete short-term config change a customer can apply to reduce impact (e.g., reduce max_tokens, prefer shorter-model variant)
- Don’t: Promise a root cause before the post-mortem or speculate about vendor causes without evidence
- Don’t: Use internal jargon (e.g., kernel selector ID, ticket SLA tiers) in customer-facing notes — keep a separate technical appendix for account engineers

Account-specific checklist for CS to run before sending message:
- Identify affected routes and models for that customer (route IDs)
- Attach one chart from telemetry (png) and a 1–2 line interpretation
- Confirm if their Dedicated or Private deployment was impacted differently and note that explicitly
- Add links to the internal incident page and expected post-mortem publish date

Escalation/handoff language for sales/AMs:
- If customer asks for immediate technical remediation beyond standard configs, loop in solutions-eng (tag: solutions-oncall) and request a joint call within 24 hours
- For customers requesting credits or contract-level impacts, escalate to GTM_revenue_ops and legal with the incident summary and timeline

Open questions / decisions needing product/eng input:
- Do we standardize an official ‘evidence packet’ (png + anonymized jitter table + commit id) for all S1s? (ops + product cost)
- How to shorten post-mortem delivery SLA for top-20 accounts without overburdening oncall?
- Can Console expose an auto-generated customer-friendly timeline slice for incidents? (product roadmap item)

Post-incident follow-up cadence (recommended):
- 0–24 hours: containment confirmation and short customer note
- 24–72 hours: internal post-mortem draft + customer-facing summary with timelines and evidence
- 72 hours–10 days: final post-mortem published; remediation plan with owners and ETA
- 30 days: follow-up with customers on remediation progress and any configuration changes applied

Templates (copyable)
- Email subject: "Update: Service incident affecting inference in [region] — resolution and next steps"
- Short email body: paste the Short status block + 1-sentence evidence summary + link to post-mortem placeholder

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc minimal and link to deeper GTM playbooks for escalation pricing and legal language
- Sync with eng on what telemetry snapshot is easiest to generate automatically
- Consider a lightweight UI button in Console that creates a tailored 'reassurance packet' for an account (auto-attach chart, timeline, PRs)

Related files / references: add links when available to incident dashboards, post-mortem templates, and the legal crediting policy.

End of kit.
